Generalizability Study (G-Study) for Multi-Facet LLM Coding

Source: R/g_study.R
g_study.Rd

Estimates crossed random-effects variance components for LLM-coded scores (e.g., unit, prompt, model, temperature, interactions, and residual) via REML (lme4::lmer) with an exact balanced-ANOVA Expected Mean Squares fallback, and computes relative Generalizability (\(E\rho^2\)) and absolute Dependability (\(\Phi\)) coefficients.

Usage

g_study(
  data,
  score_col = "score",
  id_col = "unit_id",
  facets = NULL,
  method = c("auto", "reml", "anova"),
  max_interaction = 2L,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

An llm_coded_data object produced by code_texts() or a data.frame containing unit IDs, facet columns, and numeric scores.

score_col

Name of the numeric score column. Defaults to the primary score column for llm_coded_data, or "score" otherwise.

id_col

Name of the object-of-measurement (unit/person/text) column. Default "unit_id".

facets

Optional character vector of measurement facet column names (e.g., c("prompt", "model")). If NULL, automatically detects which of c("prompt", "model", "temperature") exist in data with at least 2 distinct levels.

method

Estimation engine: "auto" (default: REML via lme4::lmer, falling back cleanly to ANOVA/EMS if REML fails), "reml", or "anova" (Brennan's Expected Mean Squares Method of Moments for balanced crossed designs).

max_interaction

Maximum random-effect interaction order to estimate separately from residual error. Default 2L (main effects and all pairwise interactions; higher-order interactions fold into residual unless replicates exist and max_interaction is increased).

na.rm

Logical; remove rows with missing score or facet values before fitting. Default TRUE.

Value

An S3 object of class "llm_g_study" with elements:

  • variance_components: tibble with component, variance, sd, pct_total, in_relative_error, in_absolute_error, facets_involved, and (for ANOVA) raw_variance.

  • g_coef, phi_coef: observed-design relative \(E\rho^2\) and absolute \(\Phi\) coefficients.

  • g_single, phi_single: single-observation reliability (all facets = 1).

  • sigma2_universe, sigma2_relative, sigma2_absolute, sem_relative, sem_absolute.

  • n_units, n_facets, n_replicates, balanced, method_used, singular, facets, id_col, score_col.

Examples

data(ema_coded)
g <- g_study(ema_coded, score_col = "llm_score", facets = c("prompt", "model"))
g
#> 
#> ── Generalizability Study (G-Study) 
#> Units (unit_id): 120 | Facets: prompt=3, model=2 | Method: REML | Balanced:
#> TRUE
#> Observed design: G (Erho^2) = 0.951 | Phi = 0.944 | SEM(rel) = 0.298, SEM(abs)
#> = 0.321
#> Single-facet (n=1): G = 0.842 | Phi = 0.821
#> # A tibble: 7 × 5
#>   component      variance     sd pct_total role                 
#>   <chr>             <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>                
#> 1 unit_id          1.74   1.32       82.1  universe             
#> 2 prompt           0.0219 0.148       1.03 absolute_only        
#> 3 model            0.005  0.0708      0.24 absolute_only        
#> 4 unit_id:prompt   0.101  0.318       4.78 relative_and_absolute
#> 5 unit_id:model    0.0525 0.229       2.48 relative_and_absolute
#> 6 prompt:model     0.0249 0.158       1.17 absolute_only        
#> 7 Residual         0.173  0.416       8.16 relative_and_absolute
